problem: Open-vocabulary object-level 3D scene graphs (ConceptGraphs, HOV-SG) merge small objects into enclosing furniture via containment association, fragment large surfaces, and use count-averaged CLIP fusion. They can only retrieve already-mapped objects and cannot recover unmapped targets or decide a target is absent.
motivation: Small, fine-grained objects lost at mapping time can never be retrieved later, which hurts embodied open-world navigation and service tasks. Geometry-only room partitions also fail in open-plan layouts, so search regions are poorly sized. A map that keeps small instances plus a tiered retrieval/exploration policy addresses both.
key_idea: Preserve small instances with symmetric-IoU plus label-aware association and area-weighted feature fusion, partition scenes by VLM-inferred function, and retrieve with a four-tier cascade (map, 2D tags, history voxel voting, active search) that can return a coverage-conditioned negative decision.
insight: Ablations show the VLM-enumeration front-end (E2G) gives most of the mAcc gain (+3.99 of 6.31), while IPSM/LAMP/AWF add +2.32 on identical detections and mainly improve instance fidelity (swallowed-class recall 15.8→43.2, PQ 0.338→0.398) and F-mIoU (AWF 50.09→61.45). The VLM backbone matters little (1.71 mAcc range across four VLMs) because final features come from area-weighted CLIP on SAM2 crops. Function-based partitioning shrinks the target-containing region (0.218 vs 0.342 for HOV-SG), though single-shot routing does not yet beat HOV-SG.
method: E2G + FAV-Gate: Kimi-k2.6 enumerates per-frame object types; a word is kept only if it recurs in at least 3 frames (minus a blacklist) and is intersected with the current frame's tags; LocateAnything boxes, SAM2 masks, CLIP features.

IPA (IPSM + LAMP): association score = (1+α)·3D IoU + (1−α)·cos(CLIP) − w_L·[label ≠ object's majority label], replacing ConceptGraphs' containment so small objects inside large ones are not absorbed; new instance if score ≤ τ (w_L=0.5).
AWF: view-area weight w = (box area/HW)·Gaussian of distance to image center (σ_v=0.6), accumulated online into a normalized weighted-mean CLIP feature.

KGSW: BEV free-space distance transform gives geometric cores by wall-dilated watershed; VLM assigns object functional types; mixed cores are split by function then DBSCAN; marker disks seed a final watershed producing functional regions and a floor-room graph.
CARA Tier 1-2: map lookup by class name / CLIP similarity, then retrieval over per-frame VLM tag features with a VLM attribute disambiguation on the best frame.

CARA Tier 3-4 + VVC: VLM picks a likely region using an ESC-style prior, a strong grounder re-runs on history frames or active waypoints (6 headings at 60°), detections are back-projected into 0.25 m voxels with ≥3-frame voting and VLM crop verification; region order is chosen by λ·S(goal|r) − (1−λ)·geodesic cost; exhausting coverage returns ∅.
Unified evaluation: all baselines re-scored with the same ConceptGraphs evaluator (52 classes, CLIP template, k=1 NN) and native Replica mesh instance PQ/SQ/RQ.

setting.backbone: Kimi-k2.6 VLM (frozen, cloud) + LocateAnything-3B grounder + SAM2 + CLIP ViT-H-14; VLM swap ablation with GPT-5.5, Claude-Sonnet-5, Qwen3.7-Plus

results: On Replica under a unified evaluator, OVIP-SG raises mAcc from 45.00 to 51.31 and F-mIoU from 56.30 to 61.45 over ConceptGraphs, and native-instance PQ from 0.338 to 0.398. KGSW reduces the target-containing region to 0.218 of the floor, and CARA reaches Top-1@1m 0.57 vs reproduced HOV-SG 0.51, and closed-loop SR 0.605 vs CLIP 0.576, with balanced negative-decision accuracy 0.773.
limitations: Retrieval and navigation gains are modest: CARA's SR advantage over CLIP is small, it is less path-efficient, and HOV-SG is better at Top-1@2-3m. KGSW's single-shot routing does not beat HOV-SG's expected cost.
The negative decision depends on coverage and annotation completeness (8 strict FPs contain target-like content), and the Tier-4 test is forced-entry on only 44 queries in two scenes.
Task B evaluation is small-scale and mostly representative cases; the real-robot evaluation is qualitative with limited quantitative detail; the system relies on cloud VLM calls.
